title: Clinical Research Essentials
description: Connect trial design choices to credible clinical evidence.

lessons.title: Controlled Trial Design
lessons.description: Understand control groups, randomization and blinding.

content.heading: Design protects the inference
content.body: Controls and randomization help separate treatment effects from alternative explanations.

lessons.title: Endpoint Strategy
lessons.description: Match study questions to meaningful endpoints.

content.heading: Begin with the decision
content.body: An endpoint is useful when it measures an outcome relevant to the scientific decision.

lessons.title: Bias and Interpretation Case
lessons.description: Identify threats to inference in a short study scenario.

nodes.body: A sponsor proposes an open-label, single-arm study for a therapy intended to reduce short-term hospitalizations. Historical admission rates vary substantially by site and season.

nodes.prompt: Which design best protects the treatment-effect inference?

choices.label: Use a concurrent randomized control group
choices.consequence: Randomization balances measured and unmeasured prognostic factors while a concurrent control captures seasonal care changes.
choices.quality: Best: addresses confounding and time trends.

choices.label: Compare only with last year's admissions
choices.consequence: Differences in sites, season and supportive care remain plausible alternative explanations.

nodes.body: The team accepts randomization. Investigators can still infer assignment from treatment monitoring requirements.
Regulators challenge the historical comparison. The team adds a concurrent randomized control, but treatment monitoring may reveal assignment.

nodes.prompt: How should the team reduce outcome-assessment bias?

choices.label: Use blinded, criteria-based hospitalization adjudication
choices.consequence: Outcome decisions are made without treatment knowledge against the same prespecified criteria.

choices.label: Let each unblinded site decide without shared criteria
choices.consequence: Knowledge of treatment and inconsistent site thresholds can influence whether an event is counted.
choices.quality: Biased: ascertainment differs by site and assignment.

nodes.body: The primary endpoint is now independently adjudicated. A mid-study review shows more missing day-30 status in the control group.

nodes.prompt: What is the most credible response to the differential missing data?

choices.label: Investigate causes and run prespecified sensitivity analyses
choices.consequence: The team quantifies how plausible missing-data assumptions affect the estimated treatment effect.
choices.quality: Best: tests whether the conclusion is robust.

choices.label: Exclude all participants with missing status
choices.consequence: A complete-case analysis may amplify bias because missingness differs between groups.
choices.quality: Incomplete: exclusion assumes the missing outcomes are ignorable.

nodes.title: A more credible treatment estimate
nodes.body: The randomized comparison, blinded adjudication and missing-data analyses support an interpretable estimate with explicit limitations.
nodes.result: Design choices protected the inference before the result was known.
